born: c. 1350 (Pinakes IRHT: c. 1350-1438; the brief says c. 1350)
died: c. 1430-1438 (dates vary: Vryonis 1970 gives 1431-1438; Pinakes gives c. 1438)
role_place: Monk of the Stoudios monastery in Constantinople; preacher; active in Crete c. 1399-1402.
why_relevant: Named in the brief as a candidate; the only Islam-linked texts I could identify are a dialogue with an 'Ishmaelite' (Argyriou 1967, UNVERIFIED second source) and a sermon chapter on the Turks as divine punishment; I could read neither Greek text, so no passage is documented.
fame: Known mainly as an anti-Latin and anti-Filioque theologian (his Procession dialogues, Bulgaris 1768 vol. A pp. 407-468). Cited on Islam chiefly by Vryonis (1970), who uses his 'Seven Times Seven Chapters' ch. 47 ('Some causes of the pains which afflict us') on the Turks as God's punishment of Christian sins, not on Islamic doctrine.

role_place: Thessalonian monk and writer; Pantokratoros monastery on Mount Athos.
why_relevant: Two anti-Islamic works are catalogued (Argyriou 1986 edition, Studi e testi 314, subject heading 'Islam--Controversial literature'); this is the strongest survey candidate, but I could not read the Greek (modern critical edition, not public domain) so no passage is documented.
fame: Known mainly as a hagiographer (Éloge by Argyriou) and anti-Latin writer; his anti-Islamic works are known largely from the 1986 critical edition and are not widely quoted in the sources I checked.

role_place: Archbishop of Thessalonica (from 1416/1417) until the Ottoman period of the city; wrote the Dialogue against all heresies.
why_relevant: His Dialogue against all heresies is reported to include polemic against Muslims; the Islamic section is not located or read.
fame: Well known for the Dialogue against all heresies and the 'One Faith' treatise; Islam content is mentioned only in summaries.

why_relevant: A patriarchal synodal letter (Migne PG 151) explains the Ishmaelite (Turkish) assault as God's chastisement for sins; historical, not doctrinal on Islam.
fame: Little cited. Known as a patriarch in the Palamite-Barlaamite period.

role_place: Constantinopolitan scholar and historian; author of the Byzantine History (Ῥωμαϊκὴ Ἱστορία).
why_relevant: His History (book 28, as cited by Fanelli 2024) describes Turkish ritual performances in the palace; the passage is a custom-description and is EXCLUDED from passages.json (see excluded.json). His dialogue with 'Agathangelos' (1352-53) is on Turkish customs.
fame: Known as the main historian of the mid-14th century and as an anti-Palamite; cited on Turks mainly as a historian, not as a theologian of Islam.

role_place: Metropolitan of Ephesus from 1329 (under Turkish rule after 1304 conquest); excommunicated 1351.
why_relevant: Vryonis (1970) says he had frequent religious debates with newly settled Muslims in Ephesus; no writing of his on Islam was identified.
fame: Known as an anti-Palamite opponent in the hesychast controversy; little known for Islam.

name_en: Theodore Agallianos (later Theophanes, metropolitan of Media)
role_place: Hieromnemon of the Patriarchate of Constantinople; theologian, writer and copyist.
why_relevant: Known for the Dialogue with a monk against the Latins (1442, ed. Blanchet 2013). A bibliography lists 'apologetic logoi of 1463' (Patrinelis 1966 ed.) that might touch Islam; UNVERIFIED.
fame: Known mainly for anti-Latin writing; Islam content unconfirmed.

role_place: Metropolitan of Ephesus; anti-unionist leader after the Council of Florence.
why_relevant: No writing on Islam found in the sources checked; his listed works are anti-Latin and liturgical/soteriological. Negative result.
fame: Very well known as the anti-unionist leader at Florence; known for anti-Latin treatises.

role_place: Thessalonian theologian (layman, nephew of Nicholas Kabasilas); anti-Latin polemicist.
why_relevant: No writing on Islam found in the sources checked; main work De processione Spiritus Sancti is anti-Latin. Negative result.
fame: Known for De processione Spiritus Sancti and anti-Latin polemic.

role_place: Patriarch of Constantinople (1353-1354, 1364-1376); author of the Life of Gregory Palamas.
why_relevant: The brief names him for his Vita of Palamas; the Vita is not in the Migne PG 151 scan I searched (that volume is a mixed conciliar and Latin-Greek collection), so its Islam content is UNVERIFIED.
fame: Known as the hagiographer of Palamas and as a patriarch; Islam content not confirmed.
